root_idea.summary: The root expresses disturbing or turning over what is concealed so that it is brought forth and exposed.
root_idea.development: The Quran-focused evidence associates بعثرة with raising and stirring up what is hidden, with a possible interpretive association with بعث and إثارة. This development describes the semantic orientation of the root, not an additional form-level meaning.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form بَعْثَرَ.

senses.definition: To bring forth and expose what is concealed beneath or within something by turning over or disturbing its covering; in the Quranic passive construction, for what is in the graves to be raised and brought out.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic attestations are passive perfect forms and concern what is in the graves. The grave context is explained as the earth being turned over and its contents brought forth; a reported interpretation focuses on buried valuables emerging before the dead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To examine or search; to seek out news or tidings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The search may be directed at a thing or at information, including searching for, after, or into news and tidings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To scatter or disperse something, turning its parts over one upon another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied classically to goods, household effects, or commodities as they are dispersed and overturned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To demolish a watering-trough or tank and turn it upside down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use referring to a watering-trough or tank that is overturned after being demolished.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers bringing out, exposing, and raising what is concealed, including the Quranic grave construction.
The search-for-news construction is included under the broader search meaning.
Covers scattering or dispersing and turning parts over one another.
Covers the specialized use for demolishing and overturning a watering-trough or tank.

cautions: The Quranic form is attested only in passive perfect forms, while the public headword is the normalized active perfect dictionary citation form.
